documents.unit: Thomas Jefferson University (student policy handbook, academic policies)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Policy)
documents.summary: A short university-wide handbook policy (created 2023) that leaves GAI use to course faculty, who state a permitted or restricted rule in the syllabus. Permitted use needs acknowledgment and student ownership; routine assistive AI is exempt; violations fall under the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy says GAI use "is under the purview of the faculty" and "documented in the course syllabus", and offers two categories, "Permitted Use of GAI" and "Restricted Use of GAI". It sets no default of its own, so the stance is delegates with those two tiers.

units.why: The Purpose section states that the policy "defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 (framework/preamble) with general phase and informs modality; it sets no rule itself.
units.anchor: defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses

units.why: The definition says "Many commonly accepted tools have artificial intelligence embedded" and that "Unless specifically prohibited, use of these tools is permissible", exempting routine features such as spell-check and search from the rules, so P100; it permits and is addressed to any individual.
units.anchor: Unless specifically prohibited, use of these tools is permissible

units.why: The definition of Generative AI as "a set of tools/algorithms capable of generating original text, images, audio, video, and computer code" sets what the policy covers, so P61 (definitions and scope), general and informs.
units.anchor: a set of tools/algorithms capable of generating original text, images, audio, video, and computer code

units.why: The definition of Permitted Use: "Authorizes use of GAI with appropriate citation in a specifically identified course and/or assignment, as determined by the course faculty". It names one of the two categories of use (permitted vs restricted), so P05 rather than P24 (citation is only part of the definition) or P04 (the main point is the category); fit is partial.
units.anchor: Authorizes use of GAI with appropriate citation in a specifically identified course and/or assignment
units.fit_note: Category definition also says permitted use requires appropriate citation and is set per course/assignment by faculty and approved by department/college.

units.why: The definition of Restricted Use: "Identifies limits around or prohibits the use of GAI in an identified course and/or assignment as determined as determined by the course faculty". The second named category in a two-way scheme, so P05; it covers both limiting and prohibiting.
units.anchor: Identifies limits around or prohibits the use of GAI in an identified course and/or assignment

units.why: The sentence "under the purview of the faculty in accordance with department, college and University policies" gives the decision on GAI use to course faculty rather than setting one rule, so P04 with instructor as actor; the document sets no default itself.
units.anchor: in a course is under the purview of the faculty
units.frag_end: University policies and is documented in the course syllabus

units.why: The same sentence adds that GAI use "is documented in the course syllabus", an expectation that faculty record the rule in the syllabus, so P09. Kept separate from the discretion rule because it is a different obligation (communication, not who decides).
units.anchor: is documented in the course syllabus

units.why: "Use of GAI beyond the approved instance and/or lacking appropriate citation is a violation of academic integrity" classifies unauthorized use as misconduct, so P36. P28 (nondisclosure as the violation) also touches the citation half, but the main point is classification as an integrity violation.
units.anchor: lacking appropriate citation is a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "This policy is applicable to all Thomas Jefferson University academic coursework both on-campus and online and at all academic levels" sets the scope, so P61 with general phase and informs.
units.anchor: applicable to all Thomas Jefferson University academic coursework both on-campus and online

units.why: Under the Components list, the instructor-stated rule "may reflect: a.) Permitted Use of GAI b.) Restricted Use of GAI", i.e. a two-category scheme of named levels, so P05 (the document lists tiers, hence stance delegates).
units.anchor: may reflect: a.) Permitted Use of GAI b.) Restricted Use of GAI

units.why: "the student will: a.) accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted" makes students owners of what they submit when GAI is permitted, so P29 with must modality.
units.anchor: accept responsibility as owner of their work submitted

units.why: The same clause adds "responsibility for the validity of the content", which makes students answerable for the correctness of AI-assisted content; closest type is P31 (verify AI output), but the text does not say to verify or that AI can err, hence fit_note.
units.anchor: accept responsibility for the validity of the content
units.fit_note: Says students answer for the validity of content but does not say AI output is often wrong or that students must verify it.

units.why: "appropriately acknowledge the use of GAI that contributed to their work even if that information is not in their final submission" requires acknowledgment of permitted GAI use, so P24; it goes beyond the type by covering contributions not visible in the final submission.
units.anchor: appropriately acknowledge the use of GAI that contributed to their work
units.fit_note: Requires acknowledging GAI that contributed to the work even when it does not appear in the final submission.

units.why: "certain standard tools may be embedded with Assistive AI technology and these may be used unless specifically prohibited" applies the routine-feature exemption to restricted or prohibited courses, so P100 (not P07, which concerns IDEs and agents).
units.anchor: these may be used unless specifically prohibited
units.frag_start: In instances where the use of GAI is restricted or prohibited
units.frag_end: may be used unless specifically prohibited

units.why: "the instructor will identify in writing those instances, if any, where the technology may be used" obliges instructors to state in writing the permitted uses under a restriction, so P09 (written statement of expectations).
units.anchor: the instructor will identify in writing those instances
units.frag_start: In instances where use of GAI

units.why: "students must adhere to the Academic Integrity Policy of the University which includes the use of GAI" binds students to the existing university policy, so P77 (comply with existing policy) rather than P36 since it does not classify any act.
units.anchor: students must adhere to the Academic Integrity Policy of the University
units.frag_start: In all instances, students must adhere

units.why: "All violations are subject to the sanctions identified in this policy" ties GAI violations to sanctions defined in the integrity policy; no specific penalties are stated here, so P36 rather than P37.
units.anchor: All violations are subject to the sanctions identified in this policy

units.why: The definition calls academic integrity "the foundation of all Jefferson teaching, learning" and "vital to advancing a culture of fairness, trust and respect", giving a fairness and honesty reason for the rules, so P95 rather than P41.
units.anchor: vital to advancing a culture of fairness, trust and respect
units.frag_start: This is the foundation of all
units.frag_end: be honest in their own work, words and ideas

units.why: "as appropriate, approved by the department and/or college" sets an approval step above the faculty decision, naming the department or college as approver, so P80 (who grants or approves); P85 is not stated.
units.anchor: as appropriate, approved by the department and/or college and documented in the course syllabus

notes: Single included document; navigation text skipped.
